name: Cham beef sausage
summary: Tung lò mò is the Cham beef sausage of Châu Đốc. VnExpress says the name is a local reading of Cham tung lamow, cow gut, and that it hangs to dry on the outskirts. Cham Muslims here skip pork, so the sausage is beef, grilled, and eaten with rice. Sour and not-sour are both sold.
origin: Cham communities in Châu Đốc. VnExpress, 2 Oct 2019, says it is a staple at religious ceremonies because pork is abstained from.
culture: VnExpress says you see the drying strings on streets away from the center. The English edition of 12 Oct 2019 shows them on a rack.
taste: The English edition says a bite brings grilled beef and fat, then sour, sweet, salty, and hot from soy sauce, basil, and pepper.
howToEat: VnExpress says the common way is to cut rounds and grill them on charcoal until they smell, then cut them smaller. Eat them with rice.
Ask for the sour one or the one that is not sour. Dip it in soy sauce, on the English edition.
A kilogram was printed at about 150,000–250,000 VND on 2 Oct 2019. Check on arrival.
where: Streets on the outskirts of Châu Đốc, where the sausages dry in front of houses. A house number was not printed. Check on arrival.
seoTitle: Tung lo mo in Chau Doc
seoDescription: Tung lò mò is the Cham beef sausage dried on the outskirts of Châu Đốc and grilled. Sour and not-sour are both sold. Check on arrival for the price.
